**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results:**

*    Total economic return was (10.6)% for the third quarter. 
*    MFA closed the quarter with $119.5 million of unrestricted cash and $241.2 million of unpledged Agency MBS. 
*    MFA paid a regular cash dividend of $0.36 per common share on October 30, 2026.

linkup.title: F.N.B. Q3 2026 EPS Rises as Net Interest Income Hits Record
linkup.snippet:
F.N.B. Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 diluted earnings per share of $0.43, up 4.9% year over year, driven by record net interest income of $376.5 million and strong balance-sheet growth. Loans and deposits expanded at annualized rates of 8.5% and 8.9%, respectively.
F.N.B. Corporation (NYSE: FNB) reported higher third-quarter 2026 earnings as record net interest income, balance-sheet growth and a wider net interest margin offset lower fee revenue and higher operating costs. The bank maintained full-year objectives calling for mid-single-digit loan and deposit growth, while forecasting net interest income of $1.485 billion to $1.500 billion. Net income for the quarter ended September 30 was $152.9 million, compared with $149.5 million a year earlier. Diluted earnings per common share increased 4.9% to $0.43 from $0.41.
Period-end loans and leases increased by $768.0 million, or 8.5% on an annualized linked-quarter basis, to $36.5 billion. Consumer loans accounted for $435.3 million of the increase, supported by residential mortgages, indirect auto loans and home-equity lines of credit.
The loan-to-deposit ratio was 92.4%, compared with 92.5% at June 30 and 90.9% a year earlier. Non-interest income fell 5.7% year over year and 4.5% sequentially to $92.6 million. Mortgage banking income declined 39.4% from a year earlier, while capital markets income fell 18.4%. Other non-interest income also decreased, partly reflecting higher equipment-lease residual gains in the preceding quarter and a recovery recorded in the year-earlier period.

octen.title: Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp (FMCC) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Net Income Jumps 17% ... By GuruFocus
octen.snippet:
- Total mortgage portfolio grew 2% year-over-year to nearly $3.7 trillion, providing $114 billion of liquidity to the U.S. housing market.
- Net worth increased 20% year-over-year to $81 billion, strengthening financial capacity to support the housing market.
- Non-interest expense decreased 6% year-over-year to nearly $2 billion, reflecting operational efficiency and expense discipline.
- Provision for credit losses increased to $800 million from $175 million in the prior year quarter, primarily due to a single-family credit reserve build from higher projected mortgage rates.
- Single-family serious delinquency rate rose 4 basis points year-over-year to 61 basis points, driven by higher delinquencies in loans originated from 2022 through 2024.
- Multifamily new business activity declined to $16 billion from $25 billion in the prior year quarter, due to elevated mortgage interest rates.
- Multifamily delinquency rate increased to 58 basis points from 51 basis points in both the prior year and prior quarter, reflecting stress from the elevated interest rate environment.
- Capital shortfall remained at $98 billion at the end of the third quarter 2026, largely because the $73 billion of senior preferred stock does not qualify as regulatory capital.
A: CFO Jim Whitlinger attributed the increase to higher net revenues from both non-interest and net interest income. Net revenues grew 19% year-over-year to $6.8 billion, driven primarily by higher non-interest income and an 8% increase in net interest income, reflecting the evolving mix of the multifamily business and continued growth of the mortgage portfolio.
